paper.title: Adversarially Robust Multi-Armed Bandit Algorithm with Variance-Dependent Regret Bounds

unmapped: losses (not rewards); loss vectors i.i.d. from a joint distribution over [0,1]^K
settings.definition_quote: In a stochastic setting, $\ell(t) $ follows an unknown distribution $\cD$ over $[0, 1]^K$, i.i.d.~for $t = 1, 2, \ldots, T$.

In the adversarial setting, we do not assume any generative models for the loss vector $\ell(t)$, but it can be chosen in an adversarial manner. More precisely, in each round, $\ell(t)$ may depend on the history of loss vectors and chosen arms

a \textit{temporary loss} $\ell'(t) \in [0, 1]^K$ is generated from an unknown distribution $\cD$, and the adversary then corrupts $\ell'(t)$ to determine $\ell(t)$. We define the \textit{corruption level} $C \geq 0$ by $C = \E [ \sum_{t=1}^T \| \ell'(t) - \ell(t) \|_{\infty} ]$.
there exists a loss distribution $\mathcal{D}$ over $[0,1]^K$ such that any consistent algorithm suffers

symbols.c_eps: constant c = O((log(1/epsilon))^2) depending on the input parameter epsilon

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: In any stochastic setting with a unique optimal arm, the proposed algorithm achieves R(T) \leq ( 2(1+\epsilon) + \sum_{i \in [K] \setminus \{ i^* \}} \max\{4\frac{\sigma_i^2}{\Delta_i} + c \log ( 1 + \frac{\sigma_i^2}{\Delta_i} ), 2(1+\epsilon)\} ) \log T + o (\log T), where ... \epsilon \in (0, 1/2] is an input parameter for the algorithm, and c = O((\log \frac{1}{\epsilon})^2).

results.notes: Bound has an o(log T) remainder, recorded as limsup of R(T) (Proposition 2 gives the precise limsup form via a function h). sigma_i^2 is the loss variance. With epsilon = 0.2 the paper numerically gets sum max{4σ²/Δ + 4.2 log(1+σ²/Δ), 2.4} + 2.4. R(T) defined as max_i E[...]; in stochastic settings equals sum Δ_i P_i.

symbols.Q_inf: min over lbar of E[sum_t ||l(t) - lbar||_inf^2]

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Further, in adversarial settings, the regret for the proposed algorithm satisfies R(T) \leq \sqrt{K \log T \min\left\{ T, 4L^*,  4 (T-L^*),  4 Q_{\infty}  \right\}} + O(K \log T) for L^* = \min_{i^* \in [K] }\E [ \sum_{t=1}^T \ell_{i^*} (t) ] and Q_{\infty} = ...

results.notes: Leading term has exact constant 1; only the K log T term is in O(). Regret is max_i E[sum l_I(t) - l_i(t)].

symbols.R_sto: RHS of the stochastic bound (2(1+eps) + sum_{i != i*} max{4 sigma_i^2/Delta_i + c log(1+sigma_i^2/Delta_i), 2(1+eps)}) log T + o(log T)

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: In addition, in corrupted stochastic settings, we have R(T) \leq \mathcal{R} + O(\sqrt{C \mathcal{R}}), where \mathcal{R} is the RHS of \eqref{eq:thm1-bound-sto}.

results.notes: Same statement restated as Proposition 3 (prop:bound-corrupted). Leading term R_sto exact; only sqrt(C R) is in O(). Regret on corrupted losses.

conditions: there exists a loss distribution D over [0,1]^K with these moments (lower bound holds for some instance)

source.label: prop_moment
source.quote: For any $0\le \mu^*<\mu_i\le 1$ and $\sigma_i^2 \le \mu_i(1-\mu_i)$, there exists a loss distribution $\mathcal{D}$ over $[0,1]^K$ such that any consistent algorithm suffers \liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac{R(T)}{\log T} \ge \sum_{i\neq i^*} \frac{\Delta_i}{...} and there exists an algorithm achieving this bound with equality for all $\mathcal{D}$.

results.notes: Simplified rephrasing of Honda & Takemura (2012) Theorem 4; mu are mean losses. Paper approximates the sup over mu as ≈ sum (2σ²/Δ + 0.5 log(1+σ²/Δ) + 1) within 6%. Achievability part is from Honda & Takemura Theorem 1.

missing_results.description: Precise limsup bound on R(T)/log T in stochastic settings for the proposed algorithm, in terms of the explicit function h(sigma_i^2/Delta_i) plus 2(1+eps). This is sharper than the max{4z + c log(1+z), 2(1+eps)} form in Theorem 1.

_verify.summary: The extraction is accurate. The settings, expressions, constants and qualifiers for Theorem 1 (stochastic, adversarial and corrupted cases), Remark 1 and Proposition 1 all match the source, and both algorithms map to the right registry entries. The only gap is Proposition 2: it gives the stochastic limsup bound in terms of the function h, which is a different expression from Theorem 1's, and the extraction mentions it only in the notes of r1.
